headings.title: Introduction and Purpose of Assessment Documentation
headings.content: Patient assessment documentation is the written or electronic legal record of nursing observations, care given, and patient responses. It serves as the primary communication tool among the multidisciplinary healthcare team to ensure continuity of care. Without clear records, vital changes in a patient's condition remain hidden between shift handovers. Beyond clinical care, these records provide data for quality improvement, nursing research, and health facility auditing across Nigerian hospitals.

headings.title: Legal, Ethical, and Professional Standards
headings.content: Nursing documentation carries immense legal weight. In a court of law, the golden rule applies: if it was not charted, it was not done. Nurses registered with the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) have a professional duty to maintain accurate, truthful records. Falsifying records or documenting care before it is actually performed constitutes professional misconduct and can lead to license revocation and legal liability.

headings.title: Core Components of a Comprehensive Assessment Record
headings.content:
A comprehensive patient record captures a holistic view of the individual. It begins with admission data, followed by vital signs, physical examination findings, and psychosocial evaluations. 

- **Subjective Data**: Symptoms and feelings reported directly by the patient using their own words.
- **Objective Data**: Measurable and observable findings gathered through physical examination, inspection, palpation, percussion, and auscultation.
- **Baseline Assessment**: The initial reference point established upon admission against which all future changes are measured.

headings.title: Principles of Accurate, Objective, and Timely Recording
headings.content: Good documentation relies on clarity, objectivity, and promptness. Nurses must avoid vague, judgmental terms such as "patient is difficult" or "looks depressed." Instead, document concrete behaviors, such as "patient refused morning medication and raised voice at staff." Always record assessments immediately after they are performed to minimize memory lapses. If an error is made on a paper record, draw a single line through it, write "mistaken entry" alongside your signature and date, and never use correction fluid.

headings.title: Types of Documentation Formats
headings.content:
Hospitals use various formats to structure nursing notes. 

| Format Type | Description | Primary Advantage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Narrative** | Paragraph style recording chronological events | Flexible, tells a sequential story |
| **SOAP/SOAPIER** | Structured as Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan... | Organizes clinical reasoning clearly |
| **PIE** | Focuses on Problem, Intervention, and Evaluation | Streamlines care planning directly into notes |
| **Charting by Exception (CBE)** | Documentation only of abnormal findings against standards | Saves time, reduces redundant paperwork |

headings.title: Common Documentation Errors and Pitfalls
headings.content: Certain recurring mistakes compromise the integrity of patient records. Delayed documentation increases the risk of forgotten details and inaccurate timelines. Charting for someone else or pre-charting actions violates basic safety protocols. Incomplete entries leave gaps that make tracking patient progress impossible. Nurses must remain vigilant against these shortcuts to maintain high standards of professional practice.

headings.title: Confidentiality, Privacy, and Data Security
headings.content: Patient records contain sensitive health information protected by ethical codes and data protection laws, such as the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation (NDPR). Nurses must never leave patient charts unattended, share computer access passwords, or discuss patient conditions in public areas like hospital corridors or cafeterias. Breaching patient confidentiality erodes trust and attracts severe legal and institutional penalties.
